# `Q-1-23` — Config Layer Parse Failure

> A configuration layer could not be validated as a coherent YAML
> configuration.

## What this means

Quarto loads configuration from several sources — `_quarto.yml`,
profile files, project metadata, document front-matter — and
merges them layer by layer. Each layer is validated for structural
soundness *before* being merged in. This error fires when one of
the layers fails that structural check.

The error message includes both the underlying problem (forwarded
from the structural validator) and a location pointing at the
configuration file in question, so you can identify which layer
failed.

## Why this happens

The error is the wrapper Quarto attaches to whatever the layer
validator complains about. Common underlying causes:

- **A tag-related error** inside the layer — for example `Q-1-24`
  (empty tag component), `Q-1-26` (invalid tag character), or
  `Q-1-28` (conflicting merge operations). The layer is otherwise
  well-formed YAML, but a tag inside it is malformed.
- **A structural inconsistency** the merger cannot reconcile, for
  example a value that should be a map appearing as a scalar in
  one layer.

## How to fix

Read the error message's "Failed to validate config layer:" detail
to see the underlying problem, then jump to the file and location
that the location field points to. The fix is whatever the
underlying error needs — `Q-1-23` itself is just the contextual
wrapper.

If the underlying error is one of the tag errors, see the page for
the specific code in the message.
